## Overview GLM-5.3-Flash on ROCm: the kpool sparse indexer (`vllm/models/glm5next/amd/sparse_indexer.py`) launches int32↔int64 casts, a `+1`, a `-1` fill and a buffer copy around `expand_pools_and_append_tail` in every sparse-attention layer. This PR lets the expand kernel read int32 pool ids and int64 positions as they are (the `+1` moves into the kernel) and write straight into `topk_indices_buffer`, removing 6 launches per sparse-attention layer, 66 per decode step. ## Claims - 1.7–4.4% lower median TPOT at 1–32 concurrent requests on 1k/1k, 8k/1k, 64k/1k and 128k/1k (MI355X, TP4, `amd/GLM-5.3-Flash-Quark-MXFP4`) against the same ROCm nightly without this PR, and 0.9–1.8% at 64; flat at 64k c16 (−0.2%), where each step carries other requests' long prefill. Two runs per arm on swapped GPU halves; every point except 128k c8 (spread larger than the change, see below) moves the same way in both runs. - A decode step issues 66 fewer kernels (1,295 → 1,229) and 308 µs less kernel time under the profiler. - Accuracy unchanged: GSM8K 0.920 vs 0.921, GPQA-Diamond 0.904 and 0.909 vs 0.914 and 0.894. - Unchanged: the NVIDIA kpool indexer, the padded (`requires_padding`) decode layout, and every other model. ## Validation Both arms: MI355X, TP4, ROCm nightly `76c6f3f2a9` (AITER v0.1.27), control = the nightly image, arm = the same nightly with this PR applied (`5786027c10`; rebased onto main since as `f493d6d757`, the same diff), nothing else. Run 1 has control on GPUs 0–3 and the arm on 4–7 of one node; run 2 swaps them on a second node. ```bash VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS=1 \ VLLM_ROCM_QUICK_REDUCE_QUANTIZATION=INT4 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_TRITON_SPARSE_MLA=1 \ vllm serve amd/GLM-5.3-Flash-Quark-MXFP4 -tp 4 --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 --reasoning-parser glm45 \ --compilation-config '{"custom_ops": ["+fused_rms_norm_gated"]}' --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 \ --max-num-seqs 256 --max-model-len 258048 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 --no-enable-prefix-caching python3 -m sglang.bench_serving --backend vllm --model amd/GLM-5.3-Flash-Quark-MXFP4 --tokenizer zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash \ --dataset-name random --random-range-ratio 1.0 --request-rate inf \ --random-input-len ISL --random-output-len 1024 --max-concurrency C --num-prompts N --warmup-requests C # 1k/1k: (C, N) = (1, 8), (2, 12), (4, 16), (8, 32), (16, 64), (32, 128), (64, 256) # 8k/1k: (1, 8), (4, 16), (16, 64), (32, 128), (64, 256) # 64k/1k: (1, 4), (4, 8), (16, 32); 128k/1k: (1, 4), (4, 8), (8, 16) ``` **Median TPOT (ms)** | workload | conc | control r1 | control r2 | #63910 r1 | #63910 r2 | change | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 8k / 1k | 1 | 6.07 | 6.13 | 5.89 | 5.93 | −3.1% | | 8k / 1k | 4 | 7.14 | 7.21 | 6.97 | 6.99 | −2.7% | | 8k / 1k | 16 | 10.24 | 10.36 | 10.05 | 10.15 | −1.9% | | 8k / 1k | 32 | 14.13 | 14.27 | 13.90 | 14.02 | −1.7% | | 8k / 1k | 64 | 20.50 | 20.67 | 20.21 | 20.60 | −0.9% | | 1k / 1k | 1 | 6.01 | 6.07 | 5.83 | 5.88 | −3.1% | | 1k / 1k | 2 | 6.55 | 6.56 | 6.34 | 6.38 | −3.0% | | 1k / 1k | 4 | 6.89 | 6.94 | 6.73 | 6.77 | −2.4% | | 1k / 1k | 8 | 7.66 | 7.73 | 7.49 | 7.50 | −2.6% | | 1k / 1k | 16 | 9.06 | 9.21 | 8.92 | 8.92 | −2.4% | | 1k / 1k | 32 | 10.74 | 10.79 | 10.50 | 10.50 | −2.5% | | 1k / 1k | 64 | 13.68 | 13.72 | 13.48 | 13.44 | −1.8% | | 64k / 1k | 1 | 6.12 | 6.18 | 5.94 | 5.98 | −3.1% | | 64k / 1k | 4 | 9.07 | 9.22 | 8.72 | 8.89 | −3.7% | | 64k / 1k | 16 | 24.64 | 25.23 | 24.62 | 25.17 | −0.2% | | 128k / 1k | 1 | 6.14 | 6.20 | 5.97 | 6.01 | −2.9% | | 128k / 1k | 4 | 11.28 | 11.59 | 10.66 | 11.20 | −4.4% | | 128k / 1k | 8 | 21.66 | 22.10 | 22.97 | 21.72 | +2.1% | The saving is a fixed ~0.2 ms a step, so it shrinks in relative terms as steps get longer (64k c16, 8k c64). 1`, so the caller's `-1` fill only covers rows after the decode rows on the uniform layout. - `_kpool_decode_update_batched_kernel` takes int64 positions (no narrowing copy). - Pool ids stay int32 (< 65k pools), so `pid * pool_size` fits. - Prefill chunks get the same direct write. ---

Thanks for the PR! A few things:
- Would it make sense to move the new test into `tests/kernels/test_kpool_decode_update_batched.py` (with a ROCm skip, since that file also runs on NVIDIA)? It already covers `kpool_compress.py` and runs in CI, while the new file isn't picked up
- GSM8K stays under `index_topk` (2048) and the GPQA prompts are short, so the prefill change isn't covered by the evals. Can you add a RULER NIAH run?
- Have you tested it with MTP on? That's the only way to hit the multi-token decode rows and the padded layout
- Have you tested how this affects gfx942 with the non-MXFP4 checkpoint?

The reference is the same kernel this PR changes, so a bug in it would show up on both sides and the test would still pass. Can you compare against `expand_pools_to_tokens` + `append_tail_to_topk` instead, like `test_tail_expansion_legacy_vs_fixed` does?

files.patch:
@@ -0,0 +1,45 @@
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""The in-place ``expand_pools_and_append_tail`` call (int32 pool ids, int64
+positions, ``seq_len_offset=1``, ``out=`` a full-width buffer row slice) writes
+the same rows as the old path (int64 ids, ``positions.to(int32) + 1``, copy into
+a ``-1``-filled buffer)."""
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from vllm.platforms import current_platform
+
+if not current_platform.is_rocm():
+    pytest.skip("AMD kpool ops", allow_module_level=True)
+
+from vllm.models.glm5next.amd.ops import kpool_compress as kpool_ops  # noqa: E402
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("rows", [1, 16, 64])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("pool_size", [4])
+def test_inplace_matches_copy_path(rows: int, pool_size: int):
+    torch.manual_seed(rows)
+    n_groups = 512
+    # topk_indices_buffer rows are wider than topk + pool_size - 1
+    width = n_groups * pool_size + 128
+    positions = torch.randint(0, 60000, (rows,), dtype=torch.int64, device="cuda")
+    seq_lens = positions + 1
+    pools = (seq_lens // pool_size).clamp(min=1)
+    rand = torch.rand(rows, n_groups, device="cuda")
+    pool_ids = (rand * pools[:, None]).to(torch.int32)
+    pool_ids[rand < 0.15] = -1  # unused top-k slots
+
+    ref_rows = kpool_ops.expand_pools_and_append_tail(
+        pool_ids.to(torch.int64), seq_lens.to(torch.int32), pool_size
+    )
+    ref = torch.full((rows, width), -1, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")
+    ref[:, : ref_rows.shape[1]] = ref_rows
+
+    buf = torch.full((rows + 3, width), 7, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")
+    kpool_ops.expand_pools_and_append_tail(
+        pool_ids, positions, pool_size, seq_len_offset=1, out=buf[:rows]
+    )
+
+    torch.testing.assert_close(buf[:rows], ref, rtol=0, atol=0)
+    assert (buf[rows:] == 7).all()  # rows past the slice are untouched

     ape_ptr,
     ape_stride_0,
     slot_mapping_ptr,  # [B, NEXT_N] int32

+    positions_ptr,  # [B, NEXT_N] int32 or int64

reviews.body:
Thanks for the PR! A few things:
- Would it make sense to move the new test into `tests/kernels/test_kpool_decode_update_batched.py` (with a ROCm skip, since that file also runs on NVIDIA)? It already covers `kpool_compress.py` and runs in CI, while the new file isn't picked up
- GSM8K stays under `index_topk` (2048) and the GPQA prompts are short, so the prefill change isn't covered by the evals. Can you add a RULER NIAH run?
- Have you tested it with MTP on? That's the only way to hit the multi-token decode rows and the padded layout
- Have you tested how this affects gfx942 with the non-MXFP4 checkpoint?
